bounded_status: RC14 checks the RC13 gateway against the library and makes what it holds durable. Replaying 23,040 recorded traces through the gateway found contract approvals ignored beside an approval store (FIND-062, fixed) and authority an application creates mid-session unreachable at the gateway (LIM-068, now carried by an operator-declared mint). The session ledger, the revocation list and the gateway's session context can live in a locked file that survives a restart and holds across processes on one machine. Four recorded gaps are closed (LIM-038 to LIM-041). Every new mechanism is opt-in; the benchmark snapshots regenerated byte-identical before the version bump. The pre-registered RC13 campaign adds bounded new evidence; the frozen RC7 evidence is carried unchanged.

material_findings.summary: Given an approval store, the monitor never consulted the contract's approved_action_fingerprints, so the gateway ignored every approval in its contract files and ENFORCE disagreed with VERIFY. It failed closed. A contract approval now counts once per session, its use recorded in the store file; a first, ledger-only version reset on a gateway restart and was replaced before release.

A deeply nested security file escaped every loader as RecursionError, and a non-UTF-8 one the library loaders as UnicodeDecodeError, so one such file in the gateway's contract directory made every lookup fail. Every unreadable security file is now a PolicyValidationError.

The adaptive attacker's feedback carried the monitor's reason codes although documented as omitting them, in 28.6% of P1b-4 episodes. The docstring is corrected and --attacker-feedback outcomes removes them; the default is unchanged.

open_surfaces.summary: Reasons are withheld from the agent by default at the gateway; the library path returns them. The RC13 campaign measured no detectable effect of the reason channel for its attacker (FIND-064), and the defaults stay (DEC-061).
Without a SessionLedger or an ApprovalStore, limits over several actions and single use of a contract-held approval remain VERIFY-only.
Model text and reasoning output are not mediated (LIM-051).
Arguments without a trust requirement carry the model's judgement inside the policy; the origin rule is a human gate, not a fix (LIM-064).
Durable state is coordinated by operating-system file locks on one machine; across machines it is not.

frozen_benchmark_evidence.interpretation: Zero observed violations is bounded evidence for the recorded campaign, not proof of universal security. SmolLM3 remains visibly gate-failed and its two target failures remain unevaluated. RC13 does not extend this evidence, the README utility aggregate is not an enforcement-cost figure, and the campaign's attacker was a deterministic mutation search rather than a language model.

lab_experiment_evidence.interpretation: Both pre-registered primary outcomes failed to validate and are reported as not evaluable. A content detector matched the enforced arm's catch rate on the exploratory family, so the separation observed is cost rather than catch rate. Results describe one application, one tool and two agent models.

rc13_campaign.interpretation: Zero protected violations with a language-model attacker across 13 local models; telling the attacker the monitor's reasons made no detectable difference (FIND-064). Episodes cluster by story, so per-episode intervals were about 2.4 times too narrow (FIND-065). Bounded evidence for this setup (LIM-069).

gateway_equivalence.interpretation: No recorded agent would have been allowed anything behind the gateway that the library refused; the one remaining difference is single use of contract approvals (FIND-063).
